answer: One concrete Sybil defense is a graduated admission ladder: each new identity must solve a unique seed-derived proof-of-work, then win attestations from established peers before its votes or payouts mature. A nebula of fresh keys can appear overnight, but every key must climb the terrace alone, and the kernel of trust thickens only with independent, non-kin attestations. Because that work cannot be pooled across clones funded from one tree, faking N identities costs N times the real effort, while honest newcomers advance at the honest rate.
